answer: If I could keep only one check, it would be Millstone dresser lintel seal carved into the paving yard ledger, because each lintel is a measured stone yield plus a guild signature, so a mason must dress cannot be faked cheaply. One proof costs 113 POA; 754 proofs cost 85202 POA, and the farm must pay before it earns anything. A real prism has a date on it, a real umber has a receipt behind it, and a real knoll has a witness beside it. The defence holds because the attacker pays and the honest agent does not.
